Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** When one-hot encoding categorical variables, each unique category in the column is transformed into a separate binary column. For example, if the 'sex' column has two categories ('male' and 'female'), it will be transformed into two columns: one for 'male' and one for 'female', where each column contains $$1$$ if the row corresponds to that category and $$0$$ otherwise.

**Hint 2:** Remember that the intercept term is an additional column in the design matrix that typically consists of all ones. This column is added to account for the baseline level of the dependent variable when all other predictors are zero. In this case, the intercept term is one of the $$8$$ columns in the design matrix $\Phi_2$.
